speed.summary: Speed work is done in 61 minutes (01:20 to 02:21). Compile and picture targets are met and the Mandelbrot and Julia drawing targets too; the Kleinian drawing target is met only while the GPU is not the limit. A new program for the opening settings now takes about 1.6 s to prepare (it was 5.4 to 9.9 s; base4 1.4 to 1.7 s), the Kleinian one about 0.6 s, and with every new feature on 2.5 s and 1.3 s. Two changes did it: main() now colours every kind of pixel through one call (pixelColour), and programs are built for what the colour settings need (trap solid code and inside colouring are left out of the source unless used, with that in the program key). With the targets met all 38 fixed scenes were pixel-identical to dist/v6a.html. After that I did optional item (a) and half of (b): trap solids now keep their colours at every quality preset; this changes the 8 fixed scenes that show a trap solid, on purpose, and the files of the unchanged-picture state are kept as out/r5/speed/*.targets-met.js. The smoke test as it was for base5 passes on my final page; tools/smoke.json itself was replaced by the page engineer at 01:47 and cannot pass on a base5 page, but it passes on a page built from all live files. Notes: notes/r5-speed.md.

names_added: pixelColour(kind, p, nor, t, d, px, hatch) in GL_COLOUR: the one colour hook main() calls; replaces surfaceColour, flatColour and cutFaceColour, which are removed
COL_HIT, COL_FLAT, COL_CUT (consts in GL_COLOUR): the kinds of pixel pixelColour is asked about (surface hit or volume sample, 2D slice pixel, cut face)
colPick(p, depth, inside, deep) in GL_COLOUR: changed, now also does what colTrapPick and colInside did (both removed); reads the palette in four places
pal(t, inside) in GL_COLOUR: changed, the palette to read is an argument; the global gColIn is removed
cOnTrap (global bool in GL_COLOUR): the renderer's gOnTrap as it stood at colourCapture()
TRAP_SOLIDS: now a preprocessor macro (0 or 1), was a const bool in GL_ORBIT; 1 means the program can draw the trap as a solid

COL_INSIDE: new macro (0 or 1); 1 means the program can colour the inside of the set (2D view, cut face). A program built with 0 declares uInMode and uCutFace as constants, and one without TRAP_SOLIDS declares uTrapSolid as a constant
TRAP_THIN: moved from GL_ORBIT to GL_HEAD, same value 2.0, now also read by trapAdd
colProgramNeeds() in 25-colour.js: returns { solid, inside } for the state in S; reads only drop-downs and tick boxes, never a dial
glNeeds(needs) in 30-shaders.js: the two #define lines that go between GL_HEAD and GL_COLOUR
glNeedsKey(needs) in 30-shaders.js: the tag '', 's', 'i' or 'si' for the program key

sceneWant(a, eq, z0, n2, klein, needs = colProgramNeeds()) in 40-render.js: sixth argument added; the key gets '|' + tag when the tag is not empty (plain keys such as 'klein' unchanged); the source includes glNeeds(needs)
sceneNow() in 40-render.js: R.sig now includes the needs tag
hit, flatPix: locals of main() in GL_TAIL, what the pixel is at the end
gOnTrap is now also set by kde() in GL_KLEIN and cleared at the top of the Kleinian de()

The scene program is now GL_HEAD + glNeeds(needs) + GL_COLOUR + (approach.glsl + GL_ORBIT | GL_KLEIN) + GL_TAIL; GL_COLOUR defines both macros as 1 when they are missing, so the old concatenation still compiles as a full program

answers_for_user: Choosing a new approach or equation is quick again. The page now takes about a second and a half to prepare one, the same as the published Version 5; before this fix the new version needed five to ten seconds.

The Mandelbrot and Julia pictures draw as fast as in Version 5 again. The Kleinian picture is a little slower than in Version 5, more so at the Fine setting, because it now measures the distance to each pearl exactly, which is what stopped small pearls coming out hollow.

Nothing changed in the pictures you have seen, with one exception that is an improvement: when the trap is the solid, it now keeps its rainbow colours at every quality setting. Before, large parts of such a solid came out plain green, most of all on Julia sets and at Fast and Ultra fast.

The first time you switch on a trap solid, an inside colouring in the 2D view, or a painted cut face, the page shows 'Preparing the formula' for one to two and a half seconds. After that, switching back and forth is immediate. Moving a dial never makes the page wait.
Saving a picture or a 3D model still gives the picture as it was when you started the job, even if you change the colour settings while it is being made.
risks: The Kleinian drawing target is missed whenever the GPU is the limit (+31 to +43 percent against base4, measured). If the release gate is measured on a busy or slow GPU, as the orchestrator's table in SPEC5 appears to have been, the Kleinian column will read about 30 percent over base4. Most of it is the exact pearl distance that was to stay.

Optional item (a) goes beyond what SPEC5 names: besides cOnTrap, trapAdd's touch record now charges the renderer's thin layer term. It changes the colours of every trap solid picture in the equation views (8 of the 40 fixed scenes, 0.3 to 3.5 percent of their pixels). I judged it an improvement on 24 scenes at 1000 x 700 in one pass; Fine was looked at in one scene only. To take it back, use out/r5/speed/25-colour.targets-met.js, 30-shaders.targets-met.js and 40-render.targets-met.js, which are the state with all 38 scenes identical to v6a.

All timings were taken on a GPU shared with the other engineer; draw times of the same page varied by a factor of two to four between runs. Compile numbers are steadier. Only this machine (Windows, ANGLE on D3D) was measured; the #if switches are plain GLSL ES 3.00 but were not tried on another driver.

More programs now exist per approach (up to four: plain, s, i, si). The cache still holds 40 and the warm-up prepares only the variant for the settings in use, so the first switch to a trap solid or inside colouring always waits for a compile.

The smoke evidence for my final page is the base5 version of the test, not the current tools/smoke.json, which checks page texts a base5 page cannot have. The joined-page run that passed the current test used the other engineer's files as they stood at 02:01, which may have changed since.

A program built without COL_INSIDE reads uCutFace as 0. I found by reading the code (not by a picture test at first) that a painted cut face with the inside left Plain needed the inside code too, and fixed colProgramNeeds; scenes 39 and 40 now cover it and are identical to v6a. Another such corner could exist in a combination the 40 scenes do not cover.

answers_for_user: Why the Sphere inversions solid fell apart away from z = 0, and whether the planes should be forced: the page now says it in your terms. The version you tested had Planes at 2, which copies the flat rule onto a second plane, and that rule jumps across one plane and tears the solid unless c is on the x-axis. The page opens with one plane, and that rule is forced: ask that lengths are squared, that the slice at z = 0 is the flat set and that angles stay true, and only this rule is left. That argument is ours, not a published theorem. Your idea that the plane should come from where the point starts is in the list as the Lathe approach; it is clean, but it gives rings where one hopes for beads.

The beaded look of Figure 4: it exists in the paper only for c on the real axis, and the paper says so itself. There is now a button, Show Figure 4, at the end of the page that sets everything up for that picture in one click, from wherever you are, and a second button, Back to one plane, to compare. Six new rules were tried to get that look for every c; judged by their pictures none works, so a Figure 4 Mandelbrot solid is an open problem, and the page says that plainly.

The third map: Use the third map in the Kleinian section is the same kind of move as the third map in the paper, the thing that lets a Kleinian group fill space. It is not the paper's group, and the squaring rules have no such switch.

The Julia list: the six entries that only look like their names with two planes now stand under their own heading, Found with two planes, after the others. Nothing was removed and your own saved points stay on top. An entry still sets only c. Beside Frame it there is a new button, As it was found, that sets the planes and iterations the entry was found with; it only appears when they differ from yours.

Saving a picture or a 3D model: both work on the test bench, but handing a file over on the published page goes through the page that hosts the lab, and that step could not be tried here.
